terminal.description: A shell in your workspace where Sefton's quote tests run on your runner.

tasks.title: Keep a list of tests
tasks.description:
Implement `test(name, fn)` in `src/runner.js`. It saves a test for later.

- it adds `{ name, fn }` to the end of the exported `tests` array, with the very function it was given
- it does not call `fn`
- when `name` is not a non-empty string, or `fn` is not a function, it throws a `TypeError` and adds nothing

The check calls `test()` with its own names and functions, then looks at `tests`.
nextSteps: Run `node tests/quote.test.js` and read the error.
Check `name` and `fn` first, and throw when either is wrong.
Add the test to the end of `tests`.
Run the file again: the error should now come from `run()`.
hints: Registering a test is only bookkeeping. Nothing about the test itself happens yet.
`typeof` tells you whether a value is a string or a function. `new TypeError('...')` is the error to throw for a value of the wrong kind.
Do both checks before `tests.push({ name, fn })`, so a bad call leaves the list as it was.

tasks.title: Run every test
tasks.description:
Implement `run()` in `src/runner.js`. It calls the function of every saved test, in the order they were added, and returns one result per test: `{ name, passed }`.

- a test passes when its function returns, whatever it returns
- a test fails when its function throws, whatever it throws
- one failure does not stop the tests after it

The check adds its own tests with your `test()`, some that return and some that throw, and reads what `run()` returns.
nextSteps: Loop over `tests` and call each function.
Call it inside a `try` so a throw lands in your `catch`.
Push a result for every test, passed or not, and return the list.
Run the file: the bulk price test should fail and the others pass.
hints: A test function has no way to report a result except by returning or throwing. Your runner has to tell those two apart for every test.
`try { ... } catch { ... }` catches anything thrown inside the `try`, including from a function you call there. Where the `try` sits decides what happens next.
Put the `try` inside the loop, around one call: `try { fn(); results.push({ name, passed: true }) } catch { results.push({ name, passed: false }) }`.

tasks.title: Keep what each test threw
tasks.description:
Make every failed result from `run()` also hold `error`: exactly the value that was thrown, not a copy and not its message.

- this holds for anything thrown: an `Error`, a string, an object, `undefined`, `null` or `''`
- a test that throws a falsy value still fails
- a passed result has no `error`

The check throws values of every kind from its own tests and compares each `error` with the value it threw.
nextSteps: Give your `catch` a name for what it caught.
Put that value on the failed result as `error`.
Make sure pass or fail is decided by whether the function threw.
Run the file and read the error on the failing test.
hints: Your report in a later issue will need the real error, so keep it whole.
`throw undefined` is legal JavaScript. If your runner decides by looking at the caught value, a falsy one looks like no error at all.
`catch (error) { results.push({ name, passed: false, error }) }` keeps the value as it is, whatever it is.
